title: Passive and Impersonal Voice in University Governance and Peer Review

sections.content: You know passive and impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6, the *ser* + past participle passive from B1 Unit 18, and how to choose among *se*, *ser* + participle, and *estar* + participle from B2 Unit 20. University bulletins, degree accreditation reports, and peer-review minutes combine all three structures to separate general procedure, named institutional agency, and final administrative status.

Use passive *se* (*se imparten seminarios*, *se otorgaron veinte becas*) when stating general academic procedures where no agent needs to be named; the verb agrees with the patient noun (*se aprobó la titulación* vs. *se aprobaron las titulaciones*). Use the process *ser* passive (*fue evaluada por el tribunal*, *fueron convocados por el rectorado*) when the institutional body performing the action is explicitly introduced with *por*. Finally, use *estar* + participle (*el programa ya está acreditado*, *la bibliografía está actualizada*) to express the resulting status once the review process is complete.

sections.title: Voice Selection in Academic Administration
rows: Se imparten cuatro asignaturas obligatorias durante el primer semestre.
La tesis doctoral fue evaluada por un tribunal de tres catedráticos.
La nueva titulación ya está acreditada para el próximo año.
Never mix *se* passive with a *por* agent (*Se evaluó la tesis por el tribunal* is non-standard).

items.english: During the conference, fifteen papers on university autonomy were presented.

items.spanish: Todas las becas de investigación ya están otorgadas y publicadas en la página del rectorado.

items.spanish: En este departamento se evita cualquier forma de plagio mediante tutorías de escritura académica.
items.english: In this department, any form of plagiarism is prevented through academic writing tutorials.

sections.content: Check participle agreement carefully: in *se* passives only the verb agrees in number (*se aprobaron las becas*), whereas in *ser* and *estar* constructions both the verb and the participle agree in gender and number with the subject (*las becas fueron otorgadas*, *las actas están firmadas*).
